blocks.title: Automation Risks and Operational Considerations comparison
Automation Risks and Operational Considerations exam shortcuts
items: One orchestration server controls everything → SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE
A central dependency can create a large operational blast radius.
Example: If the workflow engine fails, automated response stops.
Scripts were built quickly and never maintained → TECHNICAL DEBT
Old automation becomes fragile and risky.
Example: A script still uses deprecated API calls.
Workflow has too many dependencies → COMPLEXITY
More moving parts increase troubleshooting and failure modes.
Example: One response depends on five different tools and APIs.
Automation platform is expensive to license and maintain → COST
Operational benefit must justify ongoing expense.
Example: SOAR licensing and engineering exceed expected savings.
Nobody understands the workflow anymore → SUPPORTABILITY
Automation must be documented and maintainable.
Example: Staff cannot update a critical workflow after the original developer leaves.
blocks.example: First identify whether the scenario is describing an automation use case, a benefit, or an operational drawback.

questions.q: A single orchestration server controls all automated incident-response workflows. What major risk does this create?
questions.explanation: If the centralized component fails, many dependent workflows can fail with it.

questions.q: Security scripts use deprecated APIs and hard-coded credentials because they were never updated. Which issue is this?
questions.explanation: Outdated and fragile automation accumulates as technical debt.

questions.q: An automated response depends on five separate systems and APIs, making troubleshooting difficult. Which concern is this?
questions.explanation: More components and dependencies increase complexity.

questions.q: A SOAR platform requires expensive licenses and dedicated engineering staff. Which consideration is most direct?
questions.explanation: Automation can create licensing, development, and maintenance expenses.

questions.q: The employee who wrote a critical workflow leaves, and nobody understands how to maintain it. Which concern is this?
questions.explanation: Automation must remain maintainable and documented over time.
